title: How Much Does a Heat Pump Cost in the Bay Area? (2026 Pricing Guide)
summary: What a heat pump actually costs to install in the Bay Area in 2026, before and after rebates, plus the factors that swing the price and how to avoid overpaying.
body_text: If you've already called around for heat pump quotes in the Bay Area, you probably noticed that the numbers can be all over the map. One contractor says $11,000. The next says $24,000 for what sounds like the same job. It is enough to make you wonder if anyone actually knows what this costs. The price is knowable, and most of the spread you are seeing has nothing to do with your house. This guide breaks down what a heat pump really costs to install in the Bay Area in 2026, what actually moves the number up or down, and how to make sure the quote in front of you is fair. The short answer: what Bay Area homeowners actually pay for a heat pump in 2026 For a typical single-family home replacing a gas furnace with a ducted heat pump that both heats and cools, expect a range of roughly $12,000 to $22,000 before rebates, and roughly $9,000 to $19,000 after local rebates. Ductless mini-split systems for smaller homes or single rooms start lower. Here is how that breaks down by home size and system type. These are typical installed-and-permitted Bay Area ranges for 2026: System type Best for Before rebates After local rebates Ductless mini-split, single zone One room, ADU, add-on $5,000 to $8,500 $3,500 to $6,500 Ductless multi-zone (2 to 4 heads) Homes without ducts $14,000 to $26,000 $11,000 to $23,000 Ducted heat pump, ~1,000 to 1,500 sq ft Small home, furnace swap $12,000 to $16,000 $9,500 to $14,000 Ducted heat pump, ~1,750 to 2,500 sq ft Typical Bay Area home $15,000 to $20,000 $12,000 to $18,000 Ducted heat pump, 3,000+ sq ft Larger home $19,000 to $28,000 $15,000 to $25,000 Your exact number depends on the factors below and your rebate depends heavily on your city and clean energy provider, so a home in Silicon Valley Power territory can land well below these after-rebate ranges. If a quote lands far outside these ranges in either direction, we'd recommend asking some questions. Video coming soon How much does it cost to get a heat pump? What actually drives the price A heat pump quote is a stack of decisions and understanding them is how you go from feeling sold-to to being in control. Six things move the price more than anything else. 1. System size (tonnage) Heat pumps are sized in tons, and bigger is not necessarily better. An oversized unit costs more up front, wears out faster, and can heat your home unevenly. A right-sized system costs less and works better. A proper installer calculates the size from your square footage, insulation, windows, and layout. 2. Ducted versus ductless If you already have ductwork from a central furnace, a ducted heat pump can often reuse it, which keeps costs down. If your home has no ducts, you are looking at either adding ductwork or going with a ductless mini-split system, where each zone gets its own wall or ceiling unit. Ductless avoids the cost and mess of installing ducts, but multi-zone systems can add up quickly because you are paying for multiple indoor heads. 3. The condition of your ductwork Reusing ducts saves money only if the ducts are in good shape. Leaky, undersized, or aging ductwork can bleed away up to a third of your system's efficiency, so a good installer will inspect it. Sometimes the honest answer is that sealing or partial replacement is worth it. That adds cost now but saves you on every energy bill for the next fifteen years. 4. Your electrical panel A heat pump runs on electricity and older Bay Area homes often have panels that are already close to full. If your panel needs an upgrade or a new circuit to handle the outdoor unit, that is a real line item, often $1,500 to $4,000 depending on the work. Not every home needs it, and some jobs can avoid a full panel upgrade with smart electrical solutions, but it is one of the biggest swing factors between two otherwise similar quotes. Our guide to electrical panel upgrades for a heat pump covers when it is genuinely required. 5. Your existing setup and home Where the outdoor unit goes, how far the refrigerant lines have to run, whether you are removing an old gas furnace, roof versus side-yard placement, and access all factor in. A tight side yard or a second-story air handler takes more labor than a garage install. 6. Permits and your city Every legitimate Bay Area heat pump install needs a permit, and permit costs and rules vary by city. A permit might run around $100 in one jurisdiction and several hundred in another, and cities like Menlo Park , Palo Alto , and San Francisco each have their own setback rules, noise limits at the property line, and inspection requirements. This is not a place to cut corners. An unpermitted install can haunt you when you sell the home. A good installer pulls the permit for you and knows each city's process. Why Bay Area quotes swing so much Here is the part most contractors will not tell you. A large share of the price gap between quotes is not your house, but the business model on the other end of the phone. The traditional HVAC model runs on commissioned salespeople, layers of markup, and pressure. A rep is often paid to close you at the highest number you will accept. The equipment might be identical to a competitor's. The gap is sales overhead, financing kickbacks, and margin. That is the entire reason Electric Air was built differently. We quote virtually, we do not send commissioned closers, and our standard installed pricing comes in below roughly 92 percent of comparable Bay Area quotes. Rebates change the math The rebate figures below are accurate as of August 2026. These programs change their amounts, eligibility, and funding availability often, so confirm the current numbers for your address before deciding, or ask us and we will pull the latest for you. The sticker price is only half the story. California, your city, and your local clean energy provider are actively paying homeowners to switch to heat pumps, and in the Bay Area these incentives stack. Depending on where you live, that can quietly knock several thousand dollars off your installed price. Your local clean energy provider sets the base rebate: Clean energy provider Rebate WestLight Energy (San Mateo County) $1,500 per condenser, up to two, so $3,000 max Silicon Valley Clean Energy, SVCE (much of the South Bay) $2,000 per household Silicon Valley Power (Santa Clara) $3,000 per ton, up to $10,000 San Jose Clean Energy (San Jose) $1,500 MCE (parts of the East Bay and North Bay) $400 per ton, plus a $2,000 flat rebate Some cities add their own rebate on top of the provider rebate: Menlo Park : WestLight's $1,500 per condenser, plus an extra $1,500 Milpitas: SVCE's $2,000, plus an extra $2,500 Sunnyvale : SVCE's $2,000, plus an extra $1,000 Los Altos : SVCE's $2,000, plus an extra $1,000 Income-qualified programs: households that qualify can access significantly larger rebates that cover a much bigger share of the project. The paperwork is significant, but a good installer will file it for you rather than handing you a stack of forms. We cover exactly which rebates apply to your city, and how to claim them, in our guide to California heat pump rebates . How to make sure you are not overpaying You do not need to become an HVAC expert. You need to ask four questions and insist on straight answers. Ask how they sized the system. The answer should reference your home, not a generic chart. Oversizing is the most common way homeowners overpay. Ask which rebates you qualify for and who files them. If the salesperson is vague, that is a sign they are not paying attention to the thing that saves you the most money. Get more than one quote. Any honest company will let their price stand overnight. What a real Electric Air quote looks like We built our whole process around removing the friction. You share a few details about your home, we prepare an accurate estimate remotely, with every rebate you qualify for already applied. When you are ready, we confirm the details, pull your city's permit, and our own in-house crew does the install , typically in one day. We have completed more than 400 Bay Area installs this way, and we are rated 5.0 across Google and Yelp. That is the difference between a price you can trust and a number designed to be negotiated. Frequently asked questions Is a heat pump cheaper than a new furnace and air conditioner? Up front, a heat pump often costs a bit more than a basic furnace alone, but it replaces both your furnace and your AC with one system. Against a combined furnace-plus-AC replacement, a heat pump is frequently comparable or cheaper once you count rebates, and it costs less to run because it moves heat instead of burning gas to make it. Video coming soon Furnace vs Heat Pump For the full comparison, see our guide to heat pump vs furnace . How much can I save on energy bills? Heat pumps are two to three times more efficient than a gas furnace because they move heat rather than generate it. Many Bay Area homeowners see meaningful reductions in their combined heating and cooling costs, especially when replacing older equipment or electric resistance heat. Does a heat pump work in the Bay Area climate? The Bay Area is ideal for heat pumps. Winters are mild and summers are moderate, which is exactly the range where heat pumps are most efficient. Modern cold-climate models handle far harsher weather than we ever get here. How long does a heat pump last? A well-installed, right-sized heat pump typically lasts around 15 years, and often longer with basic maintenance. Correct sizing and a quality install matter more for lifespan than the brand on the box. Can I finance a heat pump? Yes. State-backed options like GoGreen California and on-bill financing from local clean energy providers can spread the cost over several years, sometimes at very low or zero interest for eligible homeowners, so you are not paying the full amount up front. The bottom line A heat pump in the Bay Area typically runs $12,000 to $22,000 before rebates and $9,000 to $19,000 after local rebates, and the biggest reason quotes differ is the sales model behind them, not your home. Know the factors that move the price and claim every rebate you are owed. Do that, and you will pay a fair price for a system that heats, cools, and cuts your bills for the next decade and a half. Want a real number for your specific home? Get a free virtual estimate with your rebates already applied, within a few minutes, no in-home sales visit required.

title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5.6 Cyber: Multimodal AI Model
summary: OpenAI officially released GPT-5.6 Cyber on August 10, 2026. The proprietary multimodal model expands OpenAI's portfolio with new capabilities.
body_text: OpenAI has expanded its model lineup with GPT-5.6 Cyber, a proprietary multimodal AI system that officially launched on August 10, 2026. The release marks another iteration in the GPT-5 series, bringing enhanced capabilities across text, image, and potentially other modalities under a specialized variant name that suggests targeted use cases. Release Date and Availability GPT-5.6 Cyber officially launched on August 10, 2026. The model is available through OpenAI's standard API infrastructure, operating under a proprietary license that restricts redistribution and requires commercial licensing agreements for enterprise deployments. Details regarding pricing tiers and access levels have not been publicly disclosed at launch, following OpenAI's typical phased rollout approach for new model variants. Multimodal Capabilities The Cyber variant operates as a multimodal system, processing and generating content across multiple input and output formats. While specific modality combinations have not been detailed in initial documentation, the designation aligns with OpenAI's broader push toward unified models that handle text, vision, and potentially audio or video streams within a single architecture. This approach reduces the need for specialized pipelines and allows for more contextually aware responses that synthesize information from diverse data types. Multimodal AI models have become the industry standard for frontier systems, enabling applications from document analysis with embedded images to complex visual reasoning tasks. GPT-5.6 Cyber's architecture likely builds on techniques established in earlier GPT-4 and GPT-5 iterations, incorporating lessons learned from real-world deployments across education, healthcare, legal, and creative sectors. The Cyber Designation The "Cyber" suffix in the model name suggests a focus on cybersecurity, digital infrastructure, or network-related tasks, though OpenAI has not released official documentation clarifying the naming convention. Industry observers speculate the variant may include specialized training data or fine-tuning for: Threat detection and security analysis workflows Code vulnerability assessment and penetration testing assistance Network traffic pattern recognition and anomaly detection Compliance documentation and regulatory interpretation Alternatively, the Cyber label could indicate enhanced capabilities for digital content moderation, synthetic media detection, or other trust and safety applications critical to online platform operations. OpenAI has historically used variant names (like "Turbo" or "Instruct") to signal performance characteristics or intended use cases rather than fundamental architectural changes. Proprietary Licensing Model GPT-5.6 Cyber operates under a proprietary license, consistent with OpenAI's approach to its most advanced models. This licensing structure grants OpenAI full control over distribution channels, usage terms, and commercial applications while generating revenue through API access fees. Enterprise customers requiring on-premises deployment or custom fine-tuning typically negotiate separate agreements with additional usage restrictions and audit requirements. The proprietary model contrasts with open-weight alternatives from competitors like Meta, Mistral, and various academic institutions, reflecting ongoing industry debates about AI accessibility versus safety controls. OpenAI has maintained that proprietary licensing allows for more rigorous safety testing, abuse prevention, and alignment research before broader release, though critics argue it concentrates power and limits research transparency. What This Means GPT-5.6 Cyber's launch demonstrates OpenAI's continued investment in specialized model variants tailored to specific industry verticals or technical domains. For organizations in cybersecurity, infrastructure management, or digital trust sectors, the model may offer performance improvements over general-purpose systems when handling domain-specific jargon, threat taxonomies, or technical documentation. However, without detailed benchmarks or capability documentation, early adopters will need to conduct internal evaluations to assess whether the Cyber variant delivers measurable advantages over existing GPT-5 models for their particular workflows. The proprietary licensing ensures OpenAI retains oversight of high-stakes applications while monetizing advanced capabilities through tiered access structures.

title: Menos de 100 días para la PAES: cómo estudiar y aprovechar el tiempo que queda
summary: Quedan menos de 100 días para la PAES Regular 2026. Descubre cómo organizar tu estudio, qué priorizar cada mes y cómo aprovechar al máximo el tiempo que queda antes del 30 de noviembre.
body_text: Quedan menos de 100 días para la PAES Regular 2026. Descubre cómo organizar tu estudio, qué priorizar y cómo aprovechar al máximo el tiempo que queda antes del 30 de noviembre. El 30 de noviembre está más cerca de lo que parece. Si hoy cuentas los días que quedan hasta la PAES Regular, probablemente te sorprenda el número. Y si todavía no has empezado a prepararte con método — o si llevas semanas estudiando sin un plan claro — este artículo es para ti. La buena noticia: menos de 100 días es tiempo suficiente para subir tu puntaje de forma real. La clave no es cuánto tiempo tienes, sino cómo lo usas. ¿Cuántos días quedan para la PAES Regular 2026? La PAES Regular 2026 se rinde los días 30 de noviembre, 1 y 2 de diciembre . Desde hoy, quedan menos de 100 días — lo que equivale a aproximadamente 14 semanas de preparación . 14 semanas bien usadas pueden marcar la diferencia entre entrar o no a la carrera que quieres. ¿Qué hacer primero? Diagnóstico antes que estudio El error más común en esta etapa es ponerse a estudiar sin saber dónde están las brechas reales. Antes de abrir un libro, necesitas responder dos preguntas: 1. ¿Cuánto necesitas? Revisa el puntaje de corte de la carrera y universidad a la que quieres postular. Esa diferencia entre tu puntaje actual y el corte es tu objetivo real. 2. ¿En qué pruebas tienes más que ganar? No todas las pruebas pesan igual en tu carrera. Identifica cuáles tienen mayor ponderación y en cuáles tienes más margen de mejora. Ahí está tu mayor retorno. 💡 Haz un ensayo diagnóstico por cada prueba que vas a rendir. No para presionarte, sino para tener datos reales de dónde estás parado hoy. Plan de estudio: cómo organizar las semanas que quedan Agosto — Semanas 1 a 4: base y diagnóstico Es el mes más importante y el que más se desperdicia. Con todo agosto por delante, muchos estudiantes lo usan "empezando de a poco" — y llegan a septiembre sin haber avanzado nada real. Usa agosto para: Hacer ensayos diagnósticos por prueba Identificar tus ejes temáticos más débiles Repasar contenidos fundamentales de cada prueba Establecer una rutina diaria de estudio (2 a 3 horas enfocadas) Septiembre — Semanas 5 a 8: práctica intensiva En septiembre la preparación se vuelve más seria. Es el momento de aumentar la intensidad y trabajar con foco en los temas donde más tienes que ganar. Usa septiembre para: Hacer al menos un ensayo completo por semana en condiciones reales Trabajar el error sistemáticamente — no basta con ver cuántas salieron mal, hay que entender por qué Reforzar los ejes temáticos nuevos del temario 2026 (Geometría en M1 y M2, Sistema Nervioso en Biología, Guerra Fría y transición democrática en Historia) Octubre — Semanas 9 a 12: simulación y afinación Octubre es el mes de la simulación. Ya deberías tener una base sólida — ahora se trata de llevar esa base al formato real de la prueba. Usa octubre para: Aumentar la frecuencia de ensayos completos (dos por semana si puedes) Practicar administración del tiempo dentro de cada prueba Identificar patrones de error que se repiten y corregirlos Noviembre — Semanas 13 y 14: consolidación y descanso estratégico Las últimas semanas no son para aprender cosas nuevas — son para consolidar lo que ya sabes y llegar en buen estado físico y mental el día de la prueba. Usa noviembre para: Mantener el ritmo sin saturarte Repasar los contenidos que más dominas para llegar confiado Cuidar el sueño, la alimentación y el descanso El día antes de cada prueba: descansa. No estudies. ¿Cuánto se puede subir en menos de 100 días? Depende de tu punto de partida, pero hay rangos realistas: Si estás bajo 500 puntos: con trabajo constante puedes subir entre 60 y 100 puntos Si estás entre 500 y 700: el rango esperable es de 30 a 60 puntos adicionales Si estás sobre 700: los avances son más finos, entre 10 y 30 puntos — pero en ese rango cada punto puede definir si quedas seleccionado o no Lo más importante: mientras antes empieces, mayor es el margen . Cada semana que pasa sin trabajar es una semana menos de progreso posible. 5 claves para aprovechar el tiempo que queda 1. Estudia por tema, no por materia completa No intentes repasar todo M1 de una vez. Identifica los ejes donde más fallas y trabájalos en profundidad, uno a la vez. 2. Haz ensayos en condiciones reales Con tiempo real, en silencio y de corrido. La PAES tiene presión de tiempo y eso también se entrena. 3. Trabaja el error, no solo el resultado Después de cada ensayo, identifica de qué temas son las preguntas que fallaste y vuelve a estudiar exactamente esos contenidos. 4. Sé constante más que intenso 2 a 3 horas de estudio enfocado todos los días rinde más que 10 horas el fin de semana seguidas de cuatro días sin estudiar. 5. No descuides el NEM Si estás en 4° Medio, tus notas del colegio todavía pueden mover tu puntaje ponderado. Un buen segundo semestre puede compensar brechas en la PAES. Preguntas frecuentes sobre preparación PAES ¿Con menos de 100 días es posible subir el puntaje? Sí, completamente. 100 días equivalen a 14 semanas de preparación — tiempo más que suficiente para subir el puntaje de forma real si se trabaja con método y consistencia. ¿Qué prueba conviene reforzar primero? Depende de tu carrera. Identifica cuál prueba tiene mayor ponderación en la fórmula de selección de la carrera que quieres y empieza por ahí. En general, Matemática M1 y Competencia Lectora tienen alta ponderación en la mayoría de las carreras. ¿Cuántas horas al día debo estudiar? Entre 2 y 3 horas de estudio enfocado al día es más efectivo que sesiones largas e irregulares. La clave es la constancia diaria. ¿Debo hacer ensayos completos o estudiar por tema? Ambos. Estudia por tema entre semana para reforzar contenidos, y haz un ensayo completo en condiciones reales al menos una vez por semana para entrenar el formato y el tiempo. ¿Cuándo debo dejar de estudiar antes de la prueba? El día antes de cada prueba, descansa. No estudies. Los contenidos que ya tienes aprendidos se consolidan mejor con sueño que con horas extra de repaso a última hora. Preu Filadd: Ultraintensivos PAES disponibles ahora Si buscas una preparación estructurada para estas últimas semanas, en el Preu Filadd lanzamos los Ultraintensivos PAES — diseñados específicamente para estudiantes que quieren aprovechar al máximo el tiempo que queda antes del 30 de noviembre. Los Ultraintensivos incluyen: Clases actualizadas al temario oficial 2026 Ejercicios por eje temático con corrección detallada Ensayos completos con análisis de resultados Seguimiento de progreso para ver cómo avanza tu puntaje semana a semana Menos de 100 días. El momento de empezar es ahora. 👉 Conoce los Ultraintensivos PAES de Filadd y empieza hoy La PAES Regular 2026 se rinde los días 30 de noviembre, 1 y 2 de diciembre de 2026.

title: OTR driver safety: 6 tips for fleet managers
summary: When managing a fleet of truck drivers for an over-the-road (OTR) company, safety is the drumbeat of your operations. You can reduce the potency of those risks by ensuring your drivers are trained, supported, […]
body_text: Share When managing a fleet of truck drivers for an over-the-road (OTR) company, safety is the drumbeat of your operations. Truck drivers are out on the road the majority of their working hours, exposing them to a high rate of risk. You can reduce the potency of those risks by ensuring your drivers are trained, supported, and equipped with all necessary resources. The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) – aiming to reduce crashes and fatalities in the trucking industry – created a list of seven Behavior Analysis and Safety Improvement Categories (BASICs). These categories are used to quantify data from OTR driving records based on a “Safety Measurement System.” The way it works is these safety categories are each given numeric values and your drivers are measured in a 0-100 range (100 indicating the worst performance). This system of measuring driver safety allows the FMCSA to intercept potential problems on the road before they occur. We looked at this list and created a list of our own: a list for fleet managers to achieve the highest level of safety from their drivers. By abiding by our six tips listed below, you can maintain the best driver scores on the BASICs safety measurement system test. And remember, the lowest scores are the best. We also created our own infographic you can hang up in your drivers’ break room that lists tips on how to be a safe driver. Read on to learn how to simply and effectively amplify safe driving habits with your team of truck drivers and win on the BASICs test. 10 safety tips infographic for your commercial drivers These are driver tips! Share with your team for compliance with stronger safety practices. Download now Six simple and effective driver safety tips to live by as a fleet manager 1. Prioritize driver training and emergency protocol When it comes to safety, knowledge is power. Providing comprehensive training programs for your drivers is essential. These programs should cover: Fleet vehicle familiarization Defensive driving techniques Traffic laws and regulations Safe loading and unloading procedures Emergency response protocols Driver wellness Encouraging ongoing training and periodic refresher courses will also help keep safety practices at the forefront of drivers’ minds. 2. Invest in regular vehicle maintenance Regular vehicle maintenance is an important part of truck driver safety. Implementing a proactive maintenance schedule ensures that trucks remain in optimal condition, reducing the risk of breakdowns and accidents. Make sure drivers are well-informed about any upcoming pre-trip inspections and establish a system for reporting issues before they become a problem. A clear and accessible inspection and reporting system will ensure all of your vehicles are perpetually optimized. 3. Encourage healthy habits for your fleet of truck drivers Driving for a long stretch of hours can take a toll on a driver’s physical and mental well-being. Promote a healthy lifestyle by emphasizing the importance of regular exercise, a balanced diet, and getting enough sleep. Encourage drivers to take regular breaks to combat fatigue and stress. In 2023, in an effort to reduce fatigued driving, the FMCSA started requiring fleet managers to provide drivers with electronic logging devices (ELDs). These devices keep a record of service hours, incentivizing fleet managers and drivers to not exceed time regulations. Implementing policies that prohibit driving under the influence is also a must as a fleet manager. The FMCSA’s Clearhouse, a secure online database, provides employers with real-time updates on drivers in the Drug and Alcohol Program, establishing a way of tracking violations and keeping the roads safe. The Drug and Alcohol Program tests and monitors FMCSA-regulated employees in accordance with federal rules against the use of controlled substances and alcohol for Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) drivers. If a violation occurs, the driver is entered into the database and receives evaluation and treatment before being cleared to operate a commercial motor vehicle (CMV) again. Employers are mandated to observe all employees and check in on them annually to ensure compliance with the rules. Ultimately, the FMCSA’s implementation of the Clearhouse is another important step towards protecting everyone on the road and keeping drivers accountable. 4. Driver check-ins and monitoring as a fleet manager Regularly assess the performance and driving behavior of your fleet of truck drivers. By providing feedback and guiding drivers on improving their driving habits, trust can be established and drivers are encouraged to perform better. This is a great opportunity to implement performance evaluations and incentives for good driving. And while cash incentives are common, many employees can be even more motivated by public acknowledgment and recognition of their work. 5. Keep the lines of communication open between you and your drivers Maintaining open communication with your drivers is another way to build a team of safe drivers. Encourage them to report immediately on safety concerns they have or difficulties they encounter on the road. Establish regular check-ins or safety meetings where drivers share their concerns and trade best practices for how to maintain safety on the road. This feedback loop will not only improve your operations but also boost your staff’s morale and engagement. It also can strengthen the bonds between drivers and managers, leading to a friendlier work environment. 6. Support your drivers by equipping them with the right tools Driver fleet card use helps streamline the financial aspects of driving, allowing your drivers to cover all essential expenses while on the road. Fleet card use can prevent drivers from experiencing any added stress that comes with money management related to their work expenses, from fuel purchases to repair costs. By minimizing the need for cash transaction or personal credit card use, drivers are able to feel more confident and secure in transactions, by reducing potential risks that come with handling cash or using multiple payment methods. The benefits of using a fleet card also go beyond payments – WEX fleet cards also give your drivers access to roadside services , like towing and jump starting. This allows your drivers to focus on their job – safe and uninterrupted driving. To learn more, please visit the company’s About WEX page . Apply for a fleet card today! Source: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration Share

title: Alight and eMed join forces to expand access to GLP-1 therapies for employers, advancing population and workforce health
body_text: Alight, Inc. (NYSE: ALIT), a leading benefits administration provider of health, wealth and leave solutions, today announced the addition of eMed Population Health, Inc. , a platform for employer-sponsored preventative health management, to the Alight Partner Network. The collaboration will enhance employer-sponsored access to GLP-1 therapies and give organizations a scalable way to support eligible employees, improve adherence to treatment and address the cost and complexity of weight management benefits. The groundswell of interest in GLP-1 medications among the general population has soared in recent years — 11% of U.S. adults now take GLP-1 medications for weight loss, up from 3% in 2024, according to Gallup's National Health and Well-Being Index . As demand for obesity and chronic condition management continues to rise, employers are seeking solutions that foster long-term workforce health while helping manage healthcare costs. By adding eMed to its Partner Network, Alight is expanding its health ecosystem with an industry-leading, flexible, outcomes-focused GLP-1 solution designed to support employers across a range of workforce health goals, benefits strategies and coverage approaches. Through a connected experience that includes clinical evaluation, treatment access, adherence support and ongoing engagement, organizations can provide eligible employees with personalized care, regardless of their coverage needs, while gaining greater visibility into utilization and outcomes. “Employers are looking for smarter, more sustainable ways to address rising healthcare costs while improving outcomes for their people,” said Jessica Borchik, SVP, Partner Strategy and Sales at Alight. “By welcoming eMed into our Partner Network, we’re expanding access to a clinically rigorous, outcomes-focused approach to GLP-1 management that helps organizations support employee health while maintaining cost control.” The collaboration reflects a shared commitment to helping employers, including Fortune 500 companies already supported by Alight, implement GLP-1 programs that align with their unique needs while improving health outcomes and managing costs. “We’re at a pivotal moment in healthcare where employers have an opportunity to fundamentally change the trajectory of population health and chronic diseases,” said Greg Page, SVP Partnerships & Strategy at eMed. “By partnering with Alight, we’re combining access and accountability in a way that helps organizations improve employee health, manage costs, and realize the full promise of GLP-1 therapies.” Together, Alight and eMed will provide employers with a scalable way to manage utilization, improve adherence and reduce avoidable healthcare spend while delivering a more connected and personalized health experience for eligible employees. To learn more about Alight’s Partner Network, visit alight.com .

title: Zscaler | Leader in 2026 Gartner SASE and SSE MQ Reports
summary: Zscaler is a Leader in 2026 Gartner SASE and SSE MQ Reports
body_text: The Zero Trust SASE Difference Gartner defines SASE platforms as “offerings that deliver converged network and security capabilities. This includes software-defined WAN (SD-WAN) and secure access to the web, cloud services and private applications regardless of the user’s location, the device used or where that application is hosted. These offerings primarily use a cloud-centric architecture delivered as a platform by one vendor" . Delivered via a cloud-native platform, customers that embrace this model expect to see significant security and operational benefits by consolidating onto a converged platform. We see that while other vendors bolted on traditional SD-WAN to their SSE offerings, at Zscaler we took a different approach. We have long maintained that legacy networking has too much implicit trust, which inevitably expands the attack surface and facilitates lateral movement of threats. This risk is further amplified today in the age of frontier AI models that can launch exploits at machine speed. If you’re reachable, you’re breachable! Zscaler’s Zero Trust SASE solution is designed from the ground up with an entirely different architecture: one that intentionally does not extend the same network connectivity to every branch and IoT device. Rooted in zero trust foundations, it securely connects users, IoT/OT devices and AI agents to the applications they need, while continuously enforced adaptive access, and without the exposed ports and lateral movement inherent to traditional networking. Branches become as simple as coffee shops , eliminating firewall complexity.

title: Bain Capital to Acquire Gong cha, one of the world’s fastest-growing tea brands, from TA Associates
summary: Bain Capital to Acquire Gong cha, one of the world’s fastest-growing tea brands, from TA Associates
body_text: TOKYO – August 6, 2026 – Bain Capital, a leading global private investment firm, today announced that it has agreed to acquire Gong cha Global (“the Company”), one of the world’s fastest-growing tea brands, from TA Associates (“TA”) and the company’s other shareholders. Gong cha, which is known around the world of its high quality, freshly brewed whole leaf tea made with premium ingredients, operates nearly 2,200 stores across 33 markets, with leading positions in key markets across Asia Pacific including Japan, Korea and Australia, alongside a growing presence across the Americas and Europe. The Company deploys a capital-light franchise model, underpinned by its Gong cha 2.0 “Digital Kitchen” – its flexible store blueprint centered around its innovative drinks dispensing technology, and serves more than 150 million beverages annually to customers. Bain Capital will work closely with Gong cha’s highly experienced management team to support the company’s next phase of growth while keeping operational excellence, and customer experience that have underpinned the brand's success. This will focus on continuing the Company’s disciplined store expansion programme in Japan and Korea, where the brand has built a highly loyal customer base and established strong brand recognition, while accelerating its growth in the United States, where Gong cha’s direct franchising model and contracted pipeline provide a multi-year runway for unit growth. Alongside this, the Company will focus on deepening customer engagement through product innovation, digital marketing, and loyalty initiatives. Bain Capital brings extensive experience in the global consumer, retail, and restaurant sectors to the partnership, including investments in Domino’s Pizza Japan, Skylark, York Holdings, Fogo de Chão, Sizzling Platter, Gail’s and Retail Zoo. The firm’s hands-on operational approach has supported franchise businesses across store development, franchisee recruitment, marketing, and supply chain efficiency. “Gong cha has built a distinctive and globally recognised brand with a loyal customer base and franchisee economics that are among the strongest in the sector. The management team’s disciplined approach to store expansion has created a strong platform with significant room to grow across Asia Pacific, including in Japan, and the Americas. We look forward to partnering with the team to support the next phase of the Group’s growth and continuing to develop its operations and marketing, which has been fundamental to its success to date,” said Naofumi Nishi, a Partner at Bain Capital. “We are grateful to TA for its partnership and shared commitment to Gong cha’s long-term success” said Paul Reynish, Global CEO of Gong cha. “TA’s investment has been instrumental in supporting our global expansion and the continued development of our business model. As we begin this next chapter with Bain Capital, we look forward to building on this momentum and bringing more high-quality whole leaf tea to consumers around the world.” “Gong cha is an excellent business with a talented leadership team and strong foundation for continued growth. We’re proud of what the team has accomplished and look forward to watching the Company’s next chapter unfold,” said Edward Sippel, Managing Director at TA. The financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Nomura Security acted as Financial Advisor to Bain Capital. J.P. Morgan and NorthPoint acted as Financial Advisors to Gong cha. title: Why Singing at Home Is One of the Easiest Ways to Reduce Stress and Support Your Immune System

body_text: Have you ever noticed how much better you feel after singing your favorite song in the shower or turning up the music during a long drive? While many people see singing as simple entertainment, research suggests it offers much more than a temporary mood boost. Whether you sing alone at home, with friends at karaoke, or as part of a local choir, singing can have a positive impact on both your mental and physical wellbeing. Scientists have found that singing may help lower stress, encourage relaxation, improve social connection, and even support parts of your immune system. The best part is that you do not need professional training or a great singing voice to enjoy these benefits. Simply singing regularly could become an easy and enjoyable wellness habit. How Singing Helps Reduce Stress One of the biggest health benefits of singing is its ability to reduce stress levels. Research has shown that singing can lower cortisol, the hormone commonly associated with stress. High cortisol levels over long periods can contribute to anxiety, poor sleep, weakened immunity, and other health concerns. Several scientific studies measured participants' saliva before and after singing sessions. The findings consistently showed noticeable reductions in cortisol after both solo singing and group singing activities. This helps explain why many people naturally feel calmer, happier, and more relaxed after singing. Singing Encourages Deep Relaxation The calming effects of singing are not only psychological. They also involve the body's nervous system. When you sing, you naturally take deep breaths and extend your exhalation while holding musical notes. This breathing pattern closely resembles breathing techniques often used during meditation and yoga. Long, slow breaths stimulate the vagus nerve, an important part of the parasympathetic nervous system. This system helps your body relax by slowing your heart rate, lowering blood pressure, and encouraging healthy digestion. As a result, singing may help move your body away from a stress response and into a calmer state. The good news is that you do not need a concert stage to experience this effect. Singing while cooking dinner, cleaning your home, or enjoying a shower may provide similar relaxation benefits. Can Singing Help Relieve Pain? Scientists have also explored whether singing affects the body's natural pain relief system. Studies suggest that singing can increase the release of endorphins, which are chemicals produced naturally by the body that help reduce pain and create feelings of happiness. Researchers measured participants' pain tolerance before and after activities such as singing, dancing, and drumming. They found that people generally had higher pain thresholds after taking part in these active musical activities. Interestingly, simply listening to music did not produce the same effect. Although more research is still needed, these findings indicate that actively participating in music may provide greater health benefits than passive listening. Singing May Strengthen Social Bonds Music has always brought people together, and science offers some explanation for why. Researchers have examined oxytocin, often called the bonding hormone because it is linked with trust and social connection. Some studies found oxytocin levels increased after group singing, while others produced mixed results. Even though hormone findings remain inconsistent, one conclusion appears repeatedly across multiple studies. People who sing together often report feeling more connected, happier, and less lonely afterward. This emotional connection may be one reason why choirs, community singing groups, and family singalongs continue to be popular across different cultures. Could Singing Support Your Immune System? Another exciting area of research focuses on the relationship between singing and immune health. One small study involving cancer patients and their caregivers found encouraging results after group singing sessions. Participants reported better moods and lower stress levels. Researchers also observed changes in cytokines, which are proteins that help regulate immune responses and inflammation. Scientists believe that reducing chronic stress may indirectly benefit the immune system because prolonged high cortisol levels are known to suppress immune function. While researchers emphasize that larger and longer-term studies are still needed, early evidence suggests singing could become part of a healthy lifestyle that supports overall wellbeing. Group Singing Versus Singing Alone Both solo and group singing offer meaningful health benefits. Singing alone provides stress relief through controlled breathing, emotional expression, and relaxation. Many people find that singing privately helps them unwind after a busy day. Group singing, however, adds another important benefit. Large community studies involving older adults found that regular choir participation helped reduce loneliness while improving mood over several months. Beyond emotional wellbeing, singing with others creates shared experiences that strengthen relationships and encourage a sense of belonging. If joining a choir is not possible, singing with friends or family can still provide many of these social benefits. Singing Is Also Good for Your Brain Your brain works surprisingly hard while you sing. Singing combines language, memory, hearing, breathing, movement, rhythm, and emotional expression all at once. Because several brain regions become active simultaneously, researchers believe singing may improve communication between different parts of the brain. Some studies suggest this increased brain activity may contribute to healthier cognitive function as people age. Although singing is not a replacement for medical treatment, it can be one enjoyable activity that supports lifelong brain health. You Do Not Need to Be a Professional Singer Many people hesitate to sing because they believe they are not talented enough. Fortunately, research indicates that the health benefits come from the act of singing itself rather than the quality of your performance. Whether you sing perfectly in tune or miss every note, your breathing, nervous system, and emotional state can still respond positively. That means anyone can make singing part of a healthy daily routine. Simple Ways to Sing More Often If you want to enjoy the possible health benefits of singing, consider making it part of your everyday life. Some easy ideas include: Sing while taking a shower. Play your favorite songs during your commute. Join a community choir. Enjoy karaoke with friends. Sing while doing household chores. Learn a new song every week. Spend a few minutes singing before bed to help relax. Even a short singing session may leave you feeling calmer and more energized. Final Thoughts Singing is far more than just entertainment. Scientific research suggests it may reduce stress, activate the body's relaxation response, increase natural feel good chemicals, encourage social connection, and potentially support immune function. Although more research is needed to fully understand every biological effect, existing evidence points toward singing as a simple, affordable, and enjoyable wellness habit. Whether you sing in the shower, the car, your kitchen, or with a local choir, your voice could be doing more for your health than you ever imagined. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional regarding any medical concerns or before making changes to your health routine. Source The Independent , July 28, 2026.

body_text: View All News New Era Energy & Digital Supports Strengthened Oversight of Data Center Development in Texas August 11, 2026 Download (opens in new window) MIDLAND, Texas, Aug. 11, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- New Era Energy & Digital, Inc. (Nasdaq: NUAI) (“New Era” or the “Company”), a developer of next-generation digital infrastructure and integrated power assets, today announced its support for Texas Governor Greg Abbott’s directive to strengthen oversight of data center development in Texas. The directive calls for greater transparency around data center power and water requirements, infrastructure costs, ownership and community impacts, and reinforces the principle that large-scale development should bring additional energy solutions to Texas rather than shift incremental cost and infrastructure burden onto Texas residents. “New Era welcomes clearer and higher standards for the industry and is fully committed to working with the Governor, regulators, utilities, ERCOT and the local community to ensure the next generation of digital infrastructure is built the right way,” said Charlie Nelson, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of New Era. “Texans must come first. For us, responsible development means paying our own way, protecting the grid and local water resources, and delivering lasting benefits for our neighbors; creating jobs, a strong tax base, and improving local communities.” New Era’s development approach is built on: Supplementing Texas power. TCDC’s power strategy is designed around dedicated energy infrastructure, including behind-the-meter generation. This reduces dependence on constrained public-grid capacity while supporting the scale and reliability required by hyperscale customers. Protecting water resources by design. TCDC’s data center design prioritizes closed-loop liquid cooling and the use of reclaimed water. New Era is also evaluating multiple independent water and wastewater solutions designed to keep produced water in productive use. Investing in the communities that host us. TCDC is expected to create significant job, training and educational opportunities through construction and ongoing operations, and to be a meaningful contributor to the local rate and tax base once complete. New Era also intends to be a part of the community, not just an investor in it – committing ongoing support for local library programs in Odessa and an after-school childcare programs serving working families. New Era believes the standards outlined in the Governor’s directive reflect the same principles on which TCDC was designed – supplementing Texas power, protecting the grid and local resources, and creating enduring value for the communities that host this infrastructure. About New Era Energy & Digital, Inc. New Era Energy & Digital is developing large-scale data centers across energy-rich U.S. markets to support AI training and inference workloads. New Era's flagship project, Texas Critical Data Centers, is a 492 acre site located in the Permian Basin, with anticipated capacity scaling to 1.4 GW over time. New Era's strategy is to combine large-acreage sites with flexible power solutions, including behind-the-meter power. New Era's approach is a modular, phased data center deployment model, utilizing best-in-class water efficiency and self-generated power to minimize community impact and accelerate time-to-power for hyperscale, enterprise and edge operators. title: Beyond the Transaction: Where Retail Media's Next Chapter Begins | Fluent
summary: Retail media's next chapter isn't about more inventory—it's about smarter signal use. Insights from Brand Innovators' Future of Retail Summit with Lowe's.
body_text: Retail media has spent years expanding its footprint. More channels, more placements, more ways to reach customers along the path to purchase. But after a day with some of retail's sharpest operators at Brand Innovators' Future of Retail and Commerce Summit, hosted with Lowe's in Charlotte, one thing was clear. The next chapter will not be defined by how much more inventory the industry can create. It will be defined by how intelligently we use the signals already there. Transaction history. Loyalty behavior. Purchase intent. Real-time context. Retailers and brands have more information than ever about what customers value and how they behave. The question is whether we are designing for it. Signals only matter if the experience reflects the moment A loyalty member completing a purchase and a first-time shopper connecting in-store are both valuable. They are not in the same mindset. A shopper who drove in specifically for the garden center on a Saturday is telling you something a banner impression never will. Each person has a different reason for being there, a different level of intent, and a different next need. The best operators use those signals to decide not only what to show, but whether the moment calls for an offer at all. That is the difference between having access to data and knowing how to use it. Experience is the driver, not the tech behind it Here is the detail that stuck with me. In an audience obsessed with AI, AI barely came up on the panels. What came up, again and again, was experience. Not the tech stack, not the targeting model, not the creative. The actual human experience of shopping. Does the interaction make the customer's life easier? Does it reduce effort? Does it help them find something useful, or does it interrupt the moment? That is also why the model only holds up when three parties win at once. The customer gets an experience that is useful and relevant. The retailer strengthens the relationship and creates incremental value. The advertiser reaches the right audience and can prove the result. Take the customer out of that equation and you can still generate short-term revenue, but you will not build anything durable. Retail media is having two conversations that belong together The industry tends to treat customer experience and business performance as separate subjects, and they are usually happening in separate rooms. One conversation is about why a moment matters. It is warm and human. It is the in-store expert, the reason a customer chose to make the trip, the interaction that earns loyalty. The people in this room understand that a store visit is not a digital failure to convert. It is a deliberate, customer-owned choice, which makes it one of the strongest intent signals a brand will ever get. The other is about proving that any of it works. It is rigorous and technical. Incrementality, new-to-brand growth, measurement a brand can actually defend. The operators on stage were blunt that reporting a conversion is not the same as proving impact, and that when measurement is not standardized across partners, brand teams end up grading their partners' homework for them. Both conversations are right. Almost no one is connecting them. That is the opportunity. The teams that will define the next chapter treat in-store moments as intent signals worth measuring, not just experiences worth delivering. They build full-funnel thinking from day one instead of starting with lower-funnel performance and backfilling brands later. And they hold their commerce media to a real bar. Not "here is a placement," but "here is what changed because of it." The transaction is a beginning, not only an outcome A transaction has always marked the end of the journey. The conversion, the completed purchase, the result everyone was working toward. It is also one of the clearest expressions of customer intent we ever get. Someone just said yes. They are engaged, they trust you, and they are open to what comes next. Most brands let that moment disappear. The opportunity is not to crowd the confirmation page with more offers. It is to recognize what the moment is worth and design for it, then measure it with the same rigor the rest of the funnel already gets. What would make the purchase more valuable? What would this customer actually appreciate next? Those are the questions that turn a transaction into a relationship. What comes next will define the channel Retail media does not have to choose between customer experience and commercial performance. Its next chapter depends on connecting them. The businesses that lead will read the customer's signals, respect the context around each interaction, and prove whether the experience changed behavior. The purchase is complete. The relationship is just beginning. Beyond the transaction? We're Fluent in that. Reach out to our team today.

title: AI consolidation: Why platforms will win and portfolios will break
summary: Our partners are proof that getting this architecture right drives real success. By building on Elastic’s unified platform rather than a fragmented portfolio, they bypass the friction of integrating d...
body_text: AI consolidation: Why platforms will win and portfolios will break By Jesse Sladek August 4, 2026 Share on Twitter Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share on LinkedIn Share on Facebook Share on Facebook Share by Email Share by Email Print this page Print As enterprises push AI into production, they’re hitting a hard ceiling: legacy data infrastructure. AI magnifies the cracks in a piecemeal IT strategy, revealing that a portfolio of bolted-together point solutions simply breaks at scale. To actually deliver ROI, AI requires a unified architecture built for massive, complex, and unstructured data. Our partners are proof that getting this architecture right drives real success. By building on Elastic’s unified platform rather than a fragmented portfolio, they bypass the friction of integrating disparate tools. This allows them to scale faster and optimize delivery, positioning themselves to capture a larger share of their customers' AI investments. The cost of waiting The promise of AI is real, but unlocking its full enterprise value takes time. This follows the J-Curve of technology adoption: a period of adjustment where companies invest, rebuild, and retrain before productivity spikes. The ones that move now on the right architecture are best equipped to close that gap. Today, too many companies are in the dip of this curve. IDC projects that by 2029, global AI infrastructure spending is forecast to exceed $1 trillion ; 1 yet, nearly half of AI-driven initiatives will miss their ROI targets in 2026 due to poor data foundations and infrastructure gaps. 2 This is one of the most common blockers we see. When AI is deployed through fragmented tools, partners spend time stitching solutions together instead of delivering differentiated value. It’s the modern equivalent of early manufacturers who bolted electric motors into factories designed around steam power, then reworked their infrastructure piece by piece to adapt. The technology’s potential is constrained by the architecture it’s plugged into. For partners deploying AI, that means unifying data models, retooling processes, and managing integrations that weren’t built to talk to one another. The added complexity lengthens the J-Curve, delaying ROI and limiting their ability to grow alongside customers. The platform benefit Compare that to Elastic’s platform approach. Our search, observability, and security offerings run on a single data layer, letting data move freely so that AI gets better context. Elastic’s advantage also comes from it being a single data store. That means unified indexing, one query layer, and one place where data actually lives together. This unified backend changes the cost model and expands capabilities. It is why Elastic was recently able to slash metrics pricing and eliminate the high-cardinality penalties competitors face — giving partners a foundation to build real services and IP on — and shortening time to value. Elastic is also open by design, giving partners the architectural flexibility to fit the solution to the problem. They can choose where to deploy and which AI or large language model (LLM) to use based on performance, risk, and cost, instead of forcing one rigid architecture onto every customer. Customers are already seeing these benefits in production. For example, PepsiCo was running 55 disparate monitoring tools before consolidating onto Elastic Observability. By unifying that architecture, they reduced hardware costs while cutting mean time to resolution (MTTR) by 30%. Colsubsidio saw a similar trajectory working with Elastic partner Insoftar. By implementing Elastic Observability, they unified logs, metrics, and traces across 40+ business processes they previously couldn't track. This cut critical incidents by 95% and MTTR by 30%. The takeaway: a unified, open platform lets partners spend less time rebuilding infrastructure and more time delivering business value. The opportunity for partners AI is driving consolidation across the industry. Customers are done shopping by feature. They’re scrutinizing architecture to determine what is built for the future versus what is simply stitched together. This shift presents a massive opportunity. Historically, buying a fragmented portfolio meant partners billed for the manual work of piecing disparate databases together. This can be a low-margin grind that limits their growth and burns through customer goodwill when ROI stalls . Elastic changes that dynamic. Because our platform provides a unified foundation for AI, partners don't need to rearchitect systems to deploy them. The payoff is twofold. First, the infrastructure is scalable, which can help deepen a partner’s footprint within their account, creating additional paths to revenue. Second, partner engagements can extend from integration work to advisory services on the business-process redesigns that successful AI demands. Fragmented portfolios force partners to do the heavy lifting of integration, while platforms let them focus on delivering value. (NYSE: BMI) ein anerkannter Innovator im Bereich Wassertechnologie. Heute kündigt das Unternehmen die Markteinführung von BlueEdge an, einer anpassbaren Suite von Lösungen, die Wasserressourcen optimiert und transparenter macht. Das in Milwaukee ansässige Unternehmen ist ein Pionier auf dem Gebiet der Durchflussmesser, von der Einführung des ersten frostsicheren Wasserzählers vor fast 120 Jahren bis hin zu den digital vernetzten Wassermanagementlösungen von heute. Das Unternehmen hat die Innovation kontinuierlich vorangetrieben und bietet nun neben fortschrittlichen Softwarelösungen auch Systeme zur Überwachung der Wasserqualität und des Wasserdrucks an. BlueEdge vereint Produkte, Software und Dienstleistungen von Badger Meter und hilft unseren Kunden, ganzheitliche Lösungen zu implementieren, um ihre Herausforderungen zu meistern. „Es ist unser Anspruch, unseren Kunden zu helfen, Wasserressourcen jetzt und für kommende Generationen effizient zu managen. Und mit der Einführung von BlueEdge gehen wir heute den logischen nächsten Schritt auf unserer Innovationsreise“, so Ken Bockhorst, Chairman, President und Chief Executive Officer von Badger Meter. BlueEdge wird von einem globalen Team unterstützt, das mit den Produkten, Softwarelösungen und Dienstleistungen rund um das Thema Wassermanagement bestens vertraut ist. Auf dieser Basis kann BlueEdge unter Berücksichtigung individueller Kundenbedürfnisse dazu beitragen, die betriebliche Effizienz zu verbessern und die Resilienz zu steigern. Die maßgeschneiderten, skalierbaren Angebote von BlueEdge sind auf die sich ändernden Anforderungen von Wasserversorgern und Industriekunden weltweit zugeschnitten und bieten Lösungen für die häufigsten Herausforderungen der Wasserwirtschaft. Dabei decken wir die Bereiche Verteilungsnetzkontrolle, Umweltüberwachung, Trinkwasseraufbereitung, Wassernutzung durch den Kunden, HLK-Systeme, industrielle Prozesse, Abwasser und Anlagenbetrieb ab. Mithilfe der BlueEdge-Lösungssuite können Kunden ihren Wasserverbrauch mit hochpräzisen und zuverlässigen Zählern, Sensoren, Instrumenten und Ventilen überwachen, die durch Echtzeitdatenerfassung und -übertragung ergänzt werden. Leistungsstarke Tools für die Softwareanalyse und Visualisierung liefern Einblicke in Wasserqualität, Nutzungsmuster, Anlagenleistung und Systemzustand. Diese Detailgenauigkeit ermöglicht zielgerichtete Maßnahmen und bietet so die Basis für die kontinuierliche Verbesserung und Erweiterung der BlueEdge-Lösung des Kunden. „Wir haben unseren Kunden zugehört und mit BlueEdge eine Architektur geschaffen, die sich an ihre sich verändernden Anforderungen anpassen lässt. Unser Expertenteam führt unsere Kunden Schritt für Schritt durch die Transformation zu einem intelligenten Wassermanagement und trägt so zum Aufbau resilienter, nachhaltiger Gemeinschaften bei“, erläutert Matt Stuyvenberg, Vice President of Software and Water Quality bei Badger Meter. Zu dieser Ankündigung hat Badger Meter ein Video veröffentlicht, das Sie hier finden: BlueEdge in der Praxis: Galveston, Texas Die auf Galveston Island gelegene texanische Stadt Galveston nutzt AMI-Netzwerk-Upgrades, um über den Zähler hinauszugehen und den Wasser- und Abwasserdruck, die Qualität und die Wasserversorgung auf der ganzen Insel zu verwalten. Nach Identifizierung der Herausforderungen implementierten die Lösungsarchitekten von Badger Meter gemeinsam mit den städtischen Betrieben die nötige Technologie zur Überwachung der Wasserqualität und des Wasserdrucks, um der Stadt Galveston einen ganzheitlichen Überblick über das Wassernetz zu verschaffen. Sensoren und Überwachungssysteme wurden dabei an strategischen Standorten installiert, um die chemische Zusammensetzung, die Klarheit und den Desinfektionsgrad der Wasserversorgung zu erfassen. Diese Daten werden direkt in BEACON® SaaS eingespeist und können zusammen mit Druck- und Verbrauchsdaten angezeigt werden. Die Betreiber können die Daten von BEACON nahezu in Echtzeit abrufen, um Chemikalien genau zu dosieren und Leitungen proaktiv zu spülen. BlueEdge hat die Systemerweiterung in Galveston vorangetrieben und bietet: Eine energieeffiziente, kosteneffektive Methode zum Ablesen von Wasserzählern Hochauflösende Daten, um potenzielle Netzprobleme zu erkennen, bevor sie zum Notfall werden Höhere Wassereinsparung Verbesserungen im Betrieb der Versorgungsunternehmen. Wo auch immer Ihr Wasser fließt, BlueEdge kann Ihnen helfen, den Betrieb mit vernetzten Geräten zu verbessern, die Ihnen wertvolle Erkenntnisse liefern. Unterstützt durch ein globales Team mit erstklassigem Service sorgt BlueEdge für zuverlässige Betriebsabläufe und verschafft Ihnen den entscheidenden Vorteil beim Wassermanagement.
